summary: The interview with Zappos COO Alfred Lin centers on how Zappos became a beloved company through a relentless focus on service, culture, and deliberate business decisions. The discussion unfolds across several documented case studies and practices: empowering customer-service reps to locate items not in stock to fulfill customer needs; a culture of belief and bottom-up leadership that prioritizes the customer experience; a controversial but defining program that pays people to leave to test commitment; the strategic use of social media (Twitter) to strengthen internal bonds and humanize the brand; a bold shift away from dropshipping to owning inventory to control the customer experience; and an evolving vision that moves from selection to service to delivering happiness. Throughout, the ROI of exceptional service is framed not just in dollars saved or earned, but in strengthened brand loyalty, employee alignment, and a durable competitive edge in tough economic times.
